text: What is the primary purpose of 'Accessor' and 'Mutator' methods?
choices: To allow controlled access to private data
explanation: When we restrict access to data by declaring them private, we write 'accessor' (getter) and 'mutator' (setter) methods to allow such data to be used or modified by others safely.

text: Which naming convention is conventionally used for a Mutator method for a variable named 'length'?
explanation: Conventionally, naming... is to capitalize the first letter of variable name and then prepend the variable name with the prefix 'set' (e.g., setLength).

text: When an object is passed as a parameter to a method, what is actually passed?
choices: A complete copy of the object
The values of its attributes only
explanation: It is to be noted that object parameters are passed by reference. So, an address (and not value) of the actual parameter is copied to formal parameter.

text: If a method modifies an object passed to it as an argument, does the change affect the original object?
choices: Yes, because the reference points to the same object
No, it only changes the local copy
Only if the object is static
Only if the method is void
explanation: Whatever modifications are performed to the object inside the method, the original object is affected as well.

text: Which keyword is used to create a subclass in Java?
explanation: In Java, to create a subclass, keyword 'extends' is used in the class definition.

text: Inheritance models which type of relationship between classes?
explanation: Inheritance models 'is-a' relationship between two classes. For example, classroom is a room.

text: Are constructors inherited by the subclass?
explanation: Note that constructors are not inherited in subclass. For example, like room, classroom also has variables... but it needs its own constructors.

text: What keyword is used to call a superclass constructor from a subclass constructor?
explanation: Keyword 'super' is used to call the constructor of superclass in the constructor of subclass.

text: When calling a superclass constructor using `super()`, where must this statement be placed?
explanation: This call must be the first statement in the constructor.

text: If a subclass constructor does not explicitly call `super()`, what happens?
choices: The compiler adds a call to the no-argument constructor of the superclass
explanation: When there is no explicit call to constructor of superclass, no-argument constructor of superclass is implicitly called as the first statement 'super()'.

text: What is 'Method Overriding'?
choices: Defining a new method with a different name
Defining a method in subclass with the same signature as in superclass
Overloading a method in the same class
Deleting a method from the superclass
explanation: When superclass and subclass have methods with same signature, a superclass method is said to be overridden in the subclass.

text: How can you call an overridden superclass method from within the subclass?
explanation: When such method of superclass is to be referred, we need to use keyword 'super' with dot operator and method name. E.g., `super.display()`.

text: If `Classroom extends Room`, which class is the 'Superclass'?
explanation: Here, room and person are called parent class (superclass); classroom and student are called child classes.

text: Are 'Private' members of a superclass accessible directly in the subclass?
choices: Only if the subclass is in the same package
explanation: Remember that private members are directly available only in the class in which they are defined and nowhere else. They are not visible even in its subclass.

text: Which access modifier makes members visible in subclasses but not to the outside world?
explanation: 'protected' members are available as 'private' members in the inherited subclass. (Context: Protected members are visible in inherited subclasses).

text: What is the relationship called when a class contains objects of another class?
explanation: Composition and aggregation are the construction of classes that incorporate other objects. They establish a 'has-a' relationship.

text: In the example `class Library { Room readingRoom; ... }`, what is the relationship between Library and Room?
explanation: There is 'has-a' relationship; 'Library' has a 'Room' used as reading room. It contains an object of class Room.

text: If `Rectangle` class has a method `isLarge(Rectangle rect)`, what is `rect`?
choices: An object passed as a parameter
explanation: For this, we may write a method where another rectangle object is passed as an argument or parameter.

text: Why might we choose Composition over Inheritance?
choices: When there is no 'is-a' relationship but a 'has-a' relationship
explanation: In this scenario, reader may think: Why not to use inheritance? ... Note that 'Library' is not of the type of 'Room'. There is 'has-a' relationship.

text: Can a subclass have its own variables in addition to the ones inherited?
choices: No, it must use only superclass variables
Yes, a subclass can add its own variables
Only if the superclass is abstract
explanation: A subclass inherits all instance variables... Note that subclass usually contains more information and methods than its superclass (e.g., nBenches added to Classroom).

text: Which memory area stores the object when a new instance is created?
explanation: Operator new allocates the memory for an object... in a special portion of memory called the heap.

text: If `Classroom` inherits `Room`, does `Classroom` inherit the `display()` method of `Room`?
choices: Only if it is declared static
Only if it is declared final
explanation: Subclass inherits all instance variables and methods from superclass. For example, subclass Classroom inherits all methods of superclass.

text: What happens if a private member of a superclass is changed to 'protected'?
choices: It becomes visible to the whole world
It becomes visible to the subclass
explanation: If we change the visibility... to private, these variables are not directly accessible... Modify... to 'protected' as follows... protected members are available in the inherited subclass.

text: In the `Library` class example, `readingRoom` is an instance of:
explanation: In 'Library' class, An object readingRoom is an attribute of class 'Room'.

text: What is the result of `rect1.area() > rect2.area()` inside a boolean method?
explanation: In the `isLarge` method example: `if (area() > rect.area()) return true; else return false;`. It compares values and returns a boolean.

text: Can a class be both a Superclass and a Subclass?
explanation: This implies Multilevel Inheritance (e.g. A extends B, B extends C). Though the text mainly shows single inheritance, the concept 'derived class or extended class' implies hierarchies.

text: Accessor methods are also known as:
explanation: Convention, accessor methods are also known as "getter" and mutator methods as "setter".

text: When a subclass overrides a method, what must remain the same?
choices: The method signature (name + parameters) and return type
explanation: Method overriding requires the methods to have the same signature (which includes name and parameters) and return type.

text: If `r1` is an object of `Room`, what is `r1` actually holding?
explanation: Variable `r1` contains a reference or address of the memory location where the new object is created.
